subsystems.name: Atomic reference
subsystems.role: provides the ultra-narrow transition that defines the clock's tick.

subsystems.name: Ultra-stable interrogation laser
subsystems.role: probes the atomic transition with an exceptionally pure and stable frequency.

subsystems.name: Optical frequency comb
subsystems.role: divides the optical frequency down to countable microwave frequencies.

subsystems.name: Control and servo electronics
subsystems.role: keeps the laser locked to the atomic resonance and steers the output.

subsystems.name: Environmental isolation
subsystems.role: shields the clock from temperature, magnetic field and vibration noise.

subsystems.name: Time transfer and comparison
subsystems.role: compares clocks at different sites to form a time scale.

buildSteps.title: Prepare the vacuum chamber
buildSteps.detail: Assemble and bake an ultra-high-vacuum chamber to remove residual gas that would collide with the atoms.

buildSteps.title: Load and cool the atoms
buildSteps.detail: Use lasers to cool atoms or ions to microkelvin temperatures and trap them in an optical lattice or Paul trap.

buildSteps.title: Build the ultra-stable laser
buildSteps.detail: Construct a stable optical cavity from ultra-low-expansion glass, mount it on vibration isolation, and lock a laser to it.

buildSteps.title: Generate the frequency comb
buildSteps.detail: Build a mode-locked femtosecond laser and broaden its spectrum in nonlinear fibre to span an octave.

buildSteps.title: Lock the laser to the atoms
buildSteps.detail: Use the comb to compare the stable laser's frequency to the atomic transition, and feedback to keep them locked.

buildSteps.title: Shield and package
buildSteps.detail: Enclose the optics and trap in thermal and magnetic shields to reduce environmental sensitivity.

buildSteps.title: Count and distribute
buildSteps.detail: Use the comb to convert the optical frequency down to a microwave signal that can be counted and compared via fibre or satellite links.

buildSteps.title: Operate and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Run the clock continuously, measure its stability, and correct for systematic shifts like gravity and magnetic field.

prerequisites.why: needed to make atoms cold enough that their motion does not smear the transition.
the probe laser must be more stable than the atomic transition to reach full precision.
only a comb can divide an optical frequency down to electronics-countable rates.
collisions with background gas shift and interrupt the atoms.
to run servos and analyse data at the required speed and precision.
to interpret clock comparisons as height differences, accurate models of Earth's gravity field are needed.

pathway.milestone: laboratory optical clocks with fractional frequency uncertainty around 10^-18, used in national metrology institutes and some field campaigns
pathway.unlocks: tests of fundamental physics and precise timekeeping.

pathway.milestone: transportable and space-based optical clocks for geodesy and navigation, and intercontinental comparisons via fibre and satellite links
pathway.unlocks: centimetre-resolution height measurement and GPS-free navigation.

pathway.milestone: redefinition of the SI second based on an optical transition, likely in the 2030s
pathway.unlocks: a more precise global time standard.

pathway.milestone: networks of optical clocks for dark matter searches and relativistic geodesy
pathway.unlocks: new probes of fundamental physics and Earth monitoring.
